weather: Showers over south-east England and the Channel, with steady rain across the rest of the country.
air: Convoy CW 3, code name Bread, was attacked off Dover in the early afternoon by about 26 Do 17s of KG 2 escorted by Bf 110s and Bf 109s. Hurricanes and Spitfires of 32, 56, 64, 74 and 111 Squadrons engaged and only one small ship was sunk. A Hurricane of 111 Squadron was lost after colliding with a Dornier. Other bombers hit shipping at Falmouth and a factory at Swansea.
home: The British Union of Fascists was declared an unlawful organisation on 10 July.
Tea went on the ration this week at 2 ounces per person per week.
The French National Assembly at Vichy voted 569 to 80 on 10 July to give full powers to Marshal Pétain.
reich: U-34 sank the Finnish steamer Petsamo and U-61 sank the Dutch steamer Alwaki on 10 July.
An OKW order signed by Keitel on 10 July called for heavy coastal batteries between Calais and Boulogne to cover a Channel crossing.
Hitler received the Hungarian Prime Minister, Count Teleki, on 10 July.

weather: Overcast over the Channel with cloud base near 5,000 feet and fair visibility, thunderstorms and bright intervals further north.
air: Ju 87s of StG 2 attacked shipping off Portland in the morning and sank the armed yacht HMS Warrior II, and 501 and 609 Squadrons lost three fighters to the escort. A second raid bombed Portland harbour just before noon, and the escorting Bf 110s of ZG 76 lost four aircraft to Hurricanes. He 111s raided Portsmouth in the early evening. A convoy off Suffolk was attacked without loss.
home: Mr R. A. Butler told the Commons on 11 July that Britain would treat Haile Selassie's Ethiopian government as an ally.
Lord Beaverbrook, Minister of Aircraft Production, appealed this week for household aluminium to be given for aircraft manufacture.
Marshal Pétain issued constitutional acts on 11 July abolishing the office of President of the French Republic.
reich: U-34 sank the Norwegian steamer Janna from convoy HX 54 on 11 July.
Grand Admiral Raeder reported to Hitler at the Berghof on 11 July and advised that a landing in England be treated as a last resort.
Romania withdrew from the League of Nations on 11 July.

weather: Mostly cloudy with early fog in the Channel and thunderstorms in many districts.
air: He 111s and Do 17s attacked convoy Booty off the Essex and Suffolk coast during the morning and were met by Hurricanes of 17, 85, 151 and 242 Squadrons. He 111s of KG 26 bombed Aberdeen at midday, killing 29 people, and 603 Squadron shot one down. Other raiders were engaged off the Isle of Wight and near Portsmouth. Bombs fell in South Wales during the night.
home: Aberdeen was bombed at midday on 12 July and 29 people were killed.
Pierre Laval was appointed Vice Premier of the French government at Vichy on 12 July.
reich: U-99 under Otto Kretschmer sank the Greek steamer Ia on 12 July and captured the Estonian steamer Merisaar.
General Jodl of the OKW wrote a memorandum on 12 July describing a landing in England as a river crossing on a broad front.

weather: Early fog over southern England cleared by the middle of the morning.
air: Shipping off Portland and Dover was the main target. Hurricanes of 238 Squadron and Spitfires of 609 Squadron met about 50 German aircraft off Portland, including Bf 110s of V./LG 1. In the late afternoon Ju 87s of StG 1 with JG 51 escort attacked a convoy off Dover and fought 56, 54 and 64 Squadrons. The destroyer HMS Vanessa was disabled by a near miss and towed into Dover.
home: Italian forces crossed from Ethiopia into Kenya on 13 July and attacked the British garrison at Moyale.
No. 302 Squadron, the first Polish fighter squadron in the RAF, was formed at Leconfield on 13 July.
reich: Hitler met Brauchitsch and Halder at the Berghof on 13 July to hear the Army's plans for a landing in England.

weather: Fair all day.
air: More than 40 Ju 87s of IV.(St)/LG 1 with Bf 109 escort attacked a convoy off Dover in the afternoon and were engaged by 151, 610 and 615 Squadrons. The coaster Island Queen was hit and later sank, and two other ships were damaged. BBC reporter Charles Gardner recorded a commentary on the fight from the cliffs. Pilot Officer Mudie of 615 Squadron was shot down and died the next day.
home: Mr Churchill said in a broadcast on the evening of 14 July that Britain would seek no terms and tolerate no parley.
General de Gaulle reviewed Free French troops in London on 14 July and laid a wreath at the statue of Marshal Foch.
The Air Ministry stated on 14 July that German ambulance seaplanes found near British shipping would fly at their own risk.
reich: U-52 sank the Greek steamer Thetis A. and the submarine UA sank the Norwegian ship Sarita on 14 July.

weather: Low cloud and worsening conditions over the Channel and southern England restricted flying.
air: Poor weather limited operations. Fifteen Do 17s of KG 2 attacked convoy Pilot in the early afternoon and were met by Hurricanes of 56 and 151 Squadrons. Single raiders bombed the Westland works at Yeovil, St Athan airfield and the Kemp Town district of Brighton. Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 off Peterhead.
home: British troops withdrew from Moyale on the Kenya frontier on 15 July.
Results were announced on 15 July for the Soviet-run elections in Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania.
reich: U-34 sank the Greek steamer Evdoxia on 15 July.
Germany moved its customs frontier on 15 July to the pre-1914 border, bringing Alsace and Lorraine inside the German customs area.

weather: Fog over northern France, the Straits of Dover and south-east England.
air: Fog kept activity low. In the afternoon Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 of KG 26 off Fraserburgh. Hurricanes of 601 Squadron intercepted Ju 88s of KG 54 and shot one down into the Solent. Night activity was mainly minelaying off the east coast.
home: The Japanese cabinet of Admiral Yonai resigned on 16 July.
The Democratic National Convention opened in Chicago on 15 July.
reich: Hitler signed Directive No. 16 on 16 July, ordering preparations for a landing operation against England.
U-61 sank the British ship Scottish Minstrel from convoy HX 55 on 16 July.

weather: Dull with occasional rain.
air: Weather again restricted flying. German aircraft searched for shipping off Scotland and the east coast. An He 111 of KG 26 and a Ju 88 of KG 51 were shot down, and a Spitfire of 64 Squadron was lost with its pilot wounded. At night bombs fell in South Wales and around the Thames Estuary while minelaying continued.
home: Britain agreed on 17 July to close the Burma Road supply route to China for three months.
reich: U-57 sank the British steamer Manipur and the Swedish steamer O.A. Brodin on 17 July, and U-43 sank the British steamer Fellside.
Grand Admiral Raeder and Field Marshal von Brauchitsch conferred on 17 July about the planned landing in England.

weather: Occasional rain in the south, cloudy over the Straits of Dover, and cool.
air: Shipping off the south and east coasts was attacked and the East Goodwin lightship was bombed and sunk. 609 Squadron lost two Spitfires to Ju 88s off Swanage, and a 610 Squadron Spitfire was shot down by Bf 109s near Calais. Bombs fell on Montrose airfield and St Athan. In the evening nine Blenheims bombed Boulogne.
home: Vichy French aircraft bombed Gibraltar on 18 July in reprisal for the British attack at Mers el Kébir.
President Roosevelt was nominated for a third term by the Democratic convention in Chicago on 18 July.
RAF Bomber Command raided the Krupp works at Essen and targets at Bremen and Hamm on the night of 18 July.
reich: Troops returning from the campaign in France paraded through the Brandenburg Gate in Berlin on 18 July.
U-99 sank the British steamer Woodbury and U-58 sank the Norwegian steamer Gyda on 18 July.

weather: Showers with bright intervals, fair over the Channel with light winds.
air: Nine Defiants of 141 Squadron on patrol off Folkestone were attacked by Bf 109s of III./JG 51 shortly after midday. Five were shot down and a sixth was written off, with heavy loss of life, before Hurricanes of 111 Squadron intervened. In the afternoon Do 17s and Ju 87s bombed Dover harbour, where the oiler War Sepoy blew up and the destroyer HMS Griffin was damaged.
home: General Sir Alan Brooke was appointed Commander in Chief, Home Forces, on 19 July.
HMAS Sydney and British destroyers sank the Italian cruiser Bartolomeo Colleoni off Cape Spada, Crete, on 19 July.
President Roosevelt accepted nomination for a third term on 19 July.
reich: Hitler addressed the Reichstag at the Kroll Opera House on 19 July and made what he called an appeal to reason directed at Britain.
At the same session Göring was promoted to Reichsmarschall and twelve generals were made field marshals.
U-62 sank the British steamer Pearlmoor from convoy SL 38 on 19 July.

weather: Occasional thunderstorms, with cloud over the Straits of Dover clearing to bright intervals.
air: Convoy Bosom was the main target as it moved east along the south coast. Around 18:00 Ju 87s of II./StG 1, escorted by Bf 109s of JG 27 and JG 51, attacked it off Dover and were met by 32, 615, 65 and 610 Squadrons. The coaster Pulborough was sunk and the destroyer HMS Brazen was hit and later sank. Two He 59 rescue seaplanes were also shot down during the day.
home: The government banned the buying and selling of new cars from 20 July.
Hitler's Reichstag speech of 19 July was rejected the same evening in an unofficial BBC German broadcast by Sefton Delmer.
reich: Ju 87 dive bombers sank the British destroyer Brazen off Dover on 20 July.
An Fw 200 Condor of KG 40 was lost over north-east England on the night of 19 to 20 July.

weather: Fine early, cloud building during the morning, fair again by evening.
air: Standing patrols covered westbound convoy CW 7 through the Straits of Dover and along the south coast. Off the Needles, 43 and 238 Squadrons met Do 17s escorted by about 50 Bf 109s and Bf 110s, and a 43 Squadron Hurricane collided with a Bf 109, killing both pilots. 238 Squadron also shot down a Do 17 and a Bf 110.
home: Britain recognised the Czechoslovak provisional government of Dr Benes in London on 21 July.
The new parliaments of Estonia, Latvia and Lithuania voted on 21 July to ask for admission to the Soviet Union.
reich: Hitler conferred with the heads of the armed services in Berlin on 21 July about a landing in England, which he called an exceptionally daring undertaking.
Göring met his senior Luftwaffe commanders at Carinhall on 21 July to discuss the air war against the RAF.
U-30 sank the British steamer Ellaroy on 21 July.

weather: Fair in the Straits, cloudy in the Channel, light westerly winds, with showers and bright intervals in the east.
air: A quiet day. Hurricanes of 145 Squadron shot down a reconnaissance Do 17 off Selsey Bill in the morning, and convoys off the east coast were attacked. Bombs on the prisoner of war camp at Duff House, Banff, killed six German prisoners. In the night of 22 to 23 July a Blenheim of the Fighter Interception Unit shot down a Do 17 off Sussex, the first success with airborne radar.
home: Lord Halifax, the Foreign Secretary, rejected Hitler's peace offer in a broadcast on the evening of 22 July.
Prince Konoye became Prime Minister of Japan on 22 July.
reich: The British Foreign Secretary, Lord Halifax, rejected the offer made in the Reichstag speech in a broadcast on 22 July.
Work began on 22 July on emplacing heavy coastal guns on the French Channel coast.

weather: Slight haze in the Straits of Dover, cloudy with occasional rain elsewhere.
air: Activity was light. Convoys off Yarmouth and Lowestoft were approached in the morning, trawlers were bombed off North Foreland and bombs fell near Pulham in Norfolk in the afternoon. A Ju 88 was shot down by 242 Squadron near Great Yarmouth. At night minelaying ran from Dover to the Forth and an He 111 was shot down near Dunbar.
home: Sir Kingsley Wood's budget of 23 July raised the standard rate of income tax to 8s 6d in the pound.
The Local Defence Volunteers were officially renamed the Home Guard on 23 July.
reich: The United States declared on 23 July that it would not recognise the Soviet annexation of the Baltic states.

weather: Cloudy over the Channel and Straits, coastal and hill fog in the west spreading east, rain in most districts.
air: Do 17s attacked convoys in the Straits of Dover and the Thames Estuary during the morning. Spitfires of 54, 65 and 610 Squadrons fought Bf 109s of JG 26 and JG 52 over Margate, and 54 Squadron lost two aircraft. A Ju 88 of KG 51 that attacked shipping in the Bristol Channel was shot down by 92 and 87 Squadrons. A lone Ju 88 bombed the Brooklands area in the afternoon.
home: Lord Beaverbrook thanked the public in a broadcast on 24 July for their part in fighter production.
The French liner Meknès, taking French naval personnel home, was torpedoed in the Channel on the night of 24 July and 416 died.
reich: The motor torpedo boat S 27 sank the French liner Meknès in the Channel on 24 July.
The submarine U-139 was commissioned on 24 July.

weather: Fine with haze in the Straits of Dover and light north-westerly winds.
air: Convoy CW 8 of 21 ships was attacked repeatedly in the Dover Straits and off Folkestone by Ju 87s and Ju 88s under heavy Bf 109 escort. Five merchant ships were sunk by air attack and the destroyers Boreas and Brilliant were damaged. Squadrons engaged included 32, 54, 64, 65, 111, 610 and 615. E-boats attacked the remaining ships that night.
home: Women and children were ordered on 25 July to leave Gibraltar.
reich: Economics Minister Walther Funk set out plans for the economic reorganisation of Europe in a speech on 25 July.
Grand Admiral Raeder told Hitler on 25 July that the Navy could not be ready for a landing before the middle of September.

weather: Heavy cloud, rain and poor visibility.
air: Poor weather kept activity down. Raids approaching Swanage, Portland and the Isle of Wight mostly turned back when fighters appeared, and 601 Squadron lost a Hurricane off the Isle of Wight. E-boats sank three ships of convoy CW 8, and the Admiralty stopped daylight merchant sailings through the Dover Strait. After midnight a Hurricane of 87 Squadron shot down an He 111 engaged in minelaying.
home: The United States placed exports of aviation fuel and some grades of scrap metal to Japan under licence on 26 July.
reich: Hitler received the Romanian Prime Minister Gigurtu and Foreign Minister Manoilescu at the Berghof on 26 July.
U-34 sank the British liner Accra and the steamer Vinemoor from convoy OB 188 on 26 July.

weather: Fair in the Straits, cloudy in the Channel, slight rain in the Midlands and over the North Sea.
air: Ju 87s with Bf 109 escort attacked a convoy off Swanage in the morning. He 111s of KG 53 sank the destroyer HMS Wren off Aldeburgh and damaged HMS Montrose. Dover harbour was raided twice in the afternoon, the destroyer leader HMS Codrington was sunk at her moorings and HMS Walpole was damaged. The Admiralty then gave up Dover as a destroyer base.
home: Japanese police arrested a number of British residents on 27 July, among them the Reuters correspondent Melville Cox.
reich: German bombers sank the British destroyers Codrington at Dover and Wren off Aldeburgh on 27 July.
U-34 sank the British ships Thiara and Sambre from convoy OB 188 on 27 July.

weather: Fine early and fair for the rest of the day, clouding over in the evening.
air: At dawn 234 Squadron shot down a Ju 88 near Plymouth. A large raid approached Dover in the early afternoon and turned away without bombing. Spitfires of 74 and 41 Squadrons fought the Bf 109 escort of JG 51, whose commander Major Werner Mölders was wounded and force landed in France. Hurricanes of 111 Squadron shot down two He 59 rescue seaplanes off Boulogne.
home: A Ju 88 came down almost undamaged near Bexhill early on 28 July and its crew was captured.
reich: Hitler received President Tiso, Prime Minister Tuka and Alexander Mach of Slovakia at the Berghof on 28 July.
Major Werner Mölders, commander of JG 51, was wounded in combat over the Channel on 28 July.
U-99 sank the British ship Auckland Star on 28 July.

weather: Fair over the whole country, hazy in the Thames Estuary and at Dover.
air: About 40 Ju 87s with some 50 Bf 109s raided Dover harbour at about 07:30 and were engaged by 41 and 501 Squadrons among others. The steamer Gronland and the yacht Gulzar were sunk and the depot ship Sandhurst was set on fire. Ju 88s attacked shipping off Dungeness and Bf 110s went for a convoy off the east coast. In the evening Ju 87s of StG 2 sank the destroyer HMS Delight off Portland.
home: Melville Cox of Reuters died on 29 July after a fall from a window while held by the Japanese military police in Tokyo.
reich: A Naval Staff memorandum of 29 July judged a mid-September landing possible but recommended postponing it to May 1941.
Dive bombers sank the British destroyer Delight off Portland on 29 July.
U-99 sank the British steamer Clan Menzies on 29 July.

weather: Unsettled with low cloud and drizzle.
air: Weather kept activity low. Raids approached convoys off Orfordness, Clacton and Harwich, and 85 Squadron shot down a Bf 110 off the Suffolk coast. Spitfires of 603 Squadron shot down an He 111 of KG 26 near Montrose. At night bombs fell in Surrey, South Wales and the Bristol area.
home: Mr Eden told the Commons on 30 July that the Home Guard would be issued with army boots as supplies allowed.
reich: Hitler instructed Göring on 30 July to prepare the Luftwaffe for a large scale air offensive against Britain.
The Naval Staff reported to the OKW on 30 July on the state of preparations for a landing in England.

weather: Fair across the country with temperatures a little above average, haze in the Channel and Straits.
air: Haze limited operations to reconnaissance and small shipping raids off the south and east coasts. At about 16:00 Bf 109s of JG 2 attacked the Dover balloon barrage and were engaged by Spitfires of 74 Squadron, which lost two pilots killed, Pilot Officer Gunn and Sergeant Eley. At night raiders from the Cherbourg area bombed South Wales and the Thames Estuary area.
home: Twenty-one American republics signed the Act of Havana on 30 July, covering European possessions in the Americas.
Vichy France decreed on 31 July the death penalty for French servicemen who join a foreign army.
reich: Hitler met Keitel, Jodl, Raeder, Brauchitsch and Halder at the Berghof on 31 July, where Raeder said the Navy could not be ready before mid-September.
U-99 sank the British steamers Jamaica Progress and Jersey City on 31 July.

weather: Fair in most districts, but the Straits and Channel were overcast, with low cloud clearing during the day.
air: German aircraft attacked shipping off the east and south coasts and reconnoitred the Channel. Hurricanes of 145 Squadron shot down a Henschel Hs 126 off Hastings and lost one pilot. In the afternoon bombers reached Norwich and hit the Boulton Paul works and railway yards. After dark, mines were laid in the Thames Estuary and off the north-east and Scottish coasts.
home: Soviet Foreign Minister Molotov told the Supreme Soviet on 1 August that the pact with Germany stood, and criticised Britain and the United States.
General de Gaulle broadcast an appeal to French Canadians for their support on 1 August.
Japanese Foreign Minister Matsuoka announced the idea of a Greater East Asia Co-Prosperity Sphere on 1 August.
reich: Hitler issued Directive No. 17 on 1 August, ordering intensified air and sea warfare against England.
Molotov reaffirmed the German-Soviet pact in a speech to the Supreme Soviet on 1 August.
U-34 sank the British submarine HMS Spearfish on 1 August.

weather: Mainly fine in the north, cloudy in the east, with a cloudy Channel and drizzle in the Dover Straits.
air: Activity was light. A convoy north of Herne Bay was bombed in the late afternoon without serious damage, and shipping off Great Yarmouth was attacked. Several formations crossed the Dover Straits in the evening but RAF squadrons failed to make contact in poor visibility. No. 303 (Polish) Squadron was formed at Northolt. Night raids reached South Wales and the Midlands.
home: A French military court sentenced General de Gaulle to death in his absence on 2 August.
Twelve Hurricanes were flown off the carrier HMS Argus to reinforce Malta on 2 August, in Operation Hurry.
The Soviet Union established the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic on 2 August.
reich: U-99 under Otto Kretschmer torpedoed and damaged three tankers of convoy OB-191 on 2 August.
A French military court sentenced Charles de Gaulle to death in absentia on 2 August.
The Soviet Union created the Moldavian Soviet Socialist Republic on 2 August after taking Bessarabia from Romania.

weather: Mainly dull with bright patches, cloud base about 4,000 feet and visibility two to five miles.
air: German activity was confined mainly to reconnaissance of shipping in the Channel and off East Anglia. Four formations of about fifteen aircraft each approached Dover in the afternoon but turned back before reaching the coast, and no interceptions were made. At night raiders flew to South Wales, with some continuing to the Liverpool, Crewe and Bradford areas.
home: Italian forces invaded British Somaliland from Italian East Africa on 3 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Lithuania on 3 August.
reich: Italian forces crossed into British Somaliland on 3 August.
U-57 sank the Swedish steamer Atos on 3 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Lithuania on 3 August.

weather: Fair to fine early, cloudy with bright intervals at midday, clearing in the evening.
air: Activity was slight. German aircraft reconnoitred the south coast and the Bristol Channel, and four small raids approached a convoy anchored in fog in St Helen's Roads off the Isle of Wight but turned away when fighters arrived. No combats were recorded. The Middle Wallop sector passed to No. 10 Group. There was little activity at night.
home: General Pershing urged in a nationwide American radio broadcast on 4 August that aid be sent to Britain.
The Royal Navy completed Operation Hurry on 4 August, having flown twelve Hurricanes to Malta from HMS Argus.
Charles Lindbergh spoke against American involvement in the war at a rally in Chicago on 4 August.
reich: U-52 sank three British ships from convoy HX-60 on 4 August.
U-58 sank the Greek steamer Pindos from convoy SL-40 on 4 August.

weather: Fine and hot, with slight haze in the Channel.
air: Shipping in the Dover Straits was the main target. In the morning Spitfires of 64 and 65 Squadrons fought Bf 109s of JG 54 off the Kent coast, and 64 Squadron lost a Spitfire and its pilot off Folkestone. In the afternoon Ju 88s escorted by Bf 109s searched for Channel shipping and were met by 41 and 151 Squadrons. At night mines were laid between the Wash and the Tay.
home: Italian forces captured the port of Zeila in British Somaliland on 5 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Latvia on 5 August.
reich: U-56 sank the British steamer Boma from convoy OB-193 on 5 August.
Italian troops occupied Zeila in British Somaliland on 5 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Latvia on 5 August.

weather: Generally cloudy with fairly strong winds and a cloud ceiling of 3,000 to 5,000 feet.
air: There was little activity. Early in the morning a single aircraft bombed the RAF station at Llandow in South Wales. Hurricanes of 85 Squadron destroyed a Dornier Do 17 that was shadowing a convoy off the east coast. Small raids plotted over the Channel turned back without attacking. At night mines were laid off the east and south-east coasts.
home: Italian forces captured Odweina in British Somaliland on 6 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Estonia on 6 August.
The American ambassador to Belgium, John Cudahy, said on 6 August that food was desperately short in Belgium and northern France.
reich: Goring and his air fleet commanders settled the strategy for the air offensive against Britain on 6 August.
The Soviet Union formally annexed Estonia on 6 August, completing its absorption of the Baltic states.
Italian troops took Odweina in British Somaliland on 6 August.

weather: Mainly fair, with cloud and thunderstorms in eastern districts and cloud in the south-east.
air: German aircraft reconnoitred convoys, and a convoy off Cromer was bombed early in the morning. Hurricanes of 46 Squadron could not intercept in thick cloud. Convoy CW 9, code name Peewit, sailed from Southend for the Channel. At night raids were widespread from the Thames Estuary to Aberdeen and from Poole to Land's End and Liverpool, and Exeter was bombed for the first time by a single aircraft.
home: Churchill and de Gaulle signed an agreement on 7 August on the organisation of the Free French forces.
Exeter was bombed for the first time on 7 August by a lone raider that did little damage.
The troopship Mohamed Ali El-Kebir was torpedoed and sunk by a U-boat on 7 August.
reich: U-38 sank the British troopship Mohamed Ali El-Kebir of 7,527 tons on 7 August.
The submarine U-140 was commissioned on 7 August.

weather: Showers and bright intervals, with a cloudy Channel.
air: Convoy CW 9 Peewit was attacked before dawn by E-boats off Sussex, then three times by Ju 87 dive bombers with strong fighter escort off the Isle of Wight and Bournemouth. About 300 German aircraft took part. Several ships were sunk, including Coquetdale and Ajax, and the convoy scattered. 145 Squadron was heavily engaged and lost five Hurricanes. A fighter sweep also crossed near Dover.
home: The Viceroy of India, Lord Linlithgow, made the August Offer on 8 August, proposing a wider Executive Council and a war advisory council.
Romania introduced anti-Jewish racial laws on 8 August.
reich: U-37 sank the British refrigerated ship Upwey Grange of 9,130 tons on 8 August.
E-boats of the 1st S-boat Flotilla from Cherbourg attacked a British Channel convoy off Sussex before dawn on 8 August.
Romania promulgated racial laws on 8 August.

weather: Cloudy with showers and some bright intervals, the Channel still cloudy.
air: The day was quiet, with isolated raids looking for east coast shipping. Late in the morning a single He 111 of KG 26 bombed Sunderland, hitting the shipyard area, and was shot down into the sea off Whitburn by 79 Squadron. At night mines were laid off the east coast, and a single aircraft dropped the first bombs on Birmingham, at Erdington.
home: Birmingham had its first air raid on 9 August when a single aircraft bombed Erdington.
A lone German bomber hit Sunderland on 9 August and was shot down off the coast by RAF fighters.
reich: The High Command issued the directive Aufbau Ost on 9 August, ordering transport and supply works in the east.
U-30 sank the Swedish motor ship Canton on 9 August.

weather: Squally and thundery with some bright intervals, the Channel cloudy.
air: Bad weather caused the planned opening of the main German air offensive to be postponed. Activity was limited to shipping and overland reconnaissance. At about 0730 a single raider crossed the coast at Pevensey and bombed the airfield at West Malling. Trawlers were machine gunned off Beachy Head. At night mines were laid.
home: The armed merchant cruiser HMS Transylvania was torpedoed and sunk west of Islay on 10 August.
Japan extended its blockade of the Chinese coast to southern China on 10 August.
reich: U-56 sank the British armed merchant cruiser Transylvania of 16,923 tons on 10 August.
Japan extended its blockade of China to the southern coast on 10 August.

weather: Fair in the morning, cloudy for most of the day.
air: About 150 aircraft crossed the coast at about 1030 in a heavy raid on Portland and Weymouth, by level and dive bombers. Fighter formations attacked the Dover balloon barrage four times during the morning. Around midday Erprobungsgruppe 210 and Do 17s attacked convoy Booty off Harwich and shipping in the Thames Estuary. Sixteen RAF squadrons were in action. At night Merseyside was raided.
home: Italian forces opened their attack on the British position at Tug Argan in Somaliland on 11 August.
Portland and Weymouth were heavily bombed on the morning of 11 August.
reich: U-38 sank the British steamer Llanfair from convoy SL-41 on 11 August.
Italian troops began the battle for the Tug Argan gap in British Somaliland on 11 August.

weather: Fine, with some mist patches.
air: Radar stations on the Kent, Sussex and Isle of Wight coasts were attacked in the morning, five being damaged and one put out of action. Convoys in the Thames Estuary were bombed, a large force raided Portsmouth and the Isle of Wight at noon, and Manston was hit by about 50 aircraft at 1245. Hawkinge and Lympne airfields were also bombed. Harassing raids were widespread at night.
home: It became an offence in the United Kingdom to waste food from 12 August.
Portsmouth was heavily raided at midday on 12 August.
reich: Italian forces continued their assault on the British position at Tug Argan in Somaliland, begun on 11 August.

weather: Mainly fair, with early mist, slight drizzle in places and some cloud in the Channel.
air: The German Eagle Day opened badly when a postponement order failed to reach Do 17s of KG 2, which bombed Eastchurch in the morning. In the afternoon raids struck Southampton, Portland, Andover and airfields in Kent and Hampshire. Ju 87s hit the Coastal Command station at Detling. The Luftwaffe flew 1,485 sorties. At night the Castle Bromwich aircraft factory was attacked.
home: An RAAF aircraft crashed near Canberra on 13 August, killing ten, including three Australian cabinet ministers and General Sir Brudenell White.
Southampton was bombed on 13 August during the heaviest day of German air attacks so far.
reich: Eleven of twelve RAF Blenheims of 82 Squadron sent to bomb Aalborg airfield in Denmark on 13 August were shot down by flak and fighters.
U-60 sank the Swedish steamer Nils Gorthon from convoy HX-62 on 13 August.
Vichy France passed a law banning secret societies on 13 August.

weather: Mainly cloudy with bright patches, and cloud in the Channel.
air: At midday raids totalling some 300 aircraft approached the Kent coast. Dover and Folkestone were dive bombed, eight Dover balloons were shot down, a lightship off Folkestone was sunk, and Bf 110s of Erprobungsgruppe 210 bombed Manston, where three Blenheims of 600 Squadron were destroyed on the ground. From 1600 small raids crossed the south-west coast. Middle Wallop and Sealand were bombed.
home: The German administrator Gustav Simon abolished the constitution of occupied Luxembourg on 14 August and made German the only official language.
British and Commonwealth troops were still holding the Tug Argan gap in Somaliland against Italian attacks on 14 August.
reich: U-59 sank the British steamer Betty on 14 August.
Gustav Simon, head of the civil administration in Luxembourg, made German the sole official language there on 14 August.

weather: Fine and warm under high pressure, with some cloud remaining over the Channel.
air: All three German air fleets attacked in five major actions. Luftflotte 5 from Norway and Denmark raided the north-east, where Ju 88s bombed Driffield, and lost heavily. In the south Hawkinge, Lympne, Martlesham Heath, Eastchurch, Middle Wallop and the Short works at Rochester were hit. In the evening Erprobungsgruppe 210 bombed Croydon in mistake for Kenley.
home: The Greek cruiser Elli was torpedoed and sunk at anchor off Tinos on 15 August.
British forces began to withdraw from the Tug Argan position in Somaliland towards Berbera on 15 August.
reich: U-51 sank the British tanker Sylvafield from convoy HX-62 on 15 August.
The Greek cruiser Elli was sunk by a submarine torpedo in the harbour of Tinos on 15 August.
The battle of Tug Argan in British Somaliland ended on 15 August with a British withdrawal.

weather: Mainly fair and warm, with haze over the Channel.
air: Two series of attacks came between 1200 and 1430 and between 1630 and 1830. Ju 87s bombed Tangmere heavily, and Gosport and the Ventnor radar station were also hit, Ventnor being put out of action. Raids on Kent and the Thames Estuary pushed towards Biggin Hill, Kenley and Hornchurch, and London had two red warnings. In the evening Brize Norton in Oxfordshire was bombed.
home: President Roosevelt disclosed on 16 August that the United States was discussing the acquisition of naval and air bases with Britain.
Airfields in Kent, Hampshire and West Sussex were bombed on 16 August, and London had two air raid warnings.
reich: U-boats attacked convoy OB-197 on 16 August, sinking the Clan Macphee and the Hedrun and damaging the Alcinous.
U-100 sank the British steamer Empire Merchant on 16 August.

weather: Fine in the Channel, with haze and some cloud in the east.
air: Despite fine weather there was little German activity beyond reconnaissance flights along the south and east coasts and over convoys. An aircraft was shot down by anti-aircraft fire at Southampton in the early morning, and a single raider dropped bombs near Hornchurch in the late afternoon. At night light raids reached the Midlands, Merseyside and South Wales.
home: The Duke of Windsor arrived in Nassau on 17 August to take up his post as Governor of the Bahamas.
Wendell Willkie formally accepted the Republican nomination for President at Elwood, Indiana, on 17 August.
British troops fought a rearguard action at Barkasan in Somaliland on 17 August to cover the evacuation from Berbera.
reich: Germany declared a total blockade of the British Isles on 17 August.
British forces in Somaliland fought a rearguard action at Barkasan on 17 August while evacuating through Berbera.

weather: Fine and fair early, cloudy for the rest of the day.
air: Around 1230 some 300 aircraft attacked Kenley, Croydon, Biggin Hill, Manston and West Malling, with Do 17s of KG 76 striking Kenley at low level. At 1400 Ju 87s and escorts attacked Gosport, Ford, Thorney Island and the Poling radar station and lost heavily. At 1700 about 200 aircraft making for Hornchurch and North Weald were turned back. London had red warnings.
home: Canada and the United States concluded the Ogdensburg Agreement on 17 August, setting up a Permanent Joint Board on Defence.
Walter Chrysler, founder of the Chrysler Corporation, died on 18 August aged 65.
reich: Italian forces in British Somaliland advanced on Berbera on 18 August as the British garrison embarked for Aden.

weather: Mainly cloudy, with occasional showers in the east.
air: The morning brought only reconnaissance. In the afternoon single aircraft bombed widely scattered targets. Ju 88s set the oil tanks at Llanreath, Pembroke Dock, on fire, and the airfields at Coltishall, Honington, Harwell and Little Rissington were attacked. Fighters destroyed a Bf 110 off Great Yarmouth and three Ju 88s in the south. At night some 60 raids were plotted and mines were laid.
home: Italian troops entered Berbera on 19 August after the British garrison of Somaliland had been evacuated by sea to Aden.
Oil tanks at Pembroke Dock were set on fire by German bombers on 19 August.
reich: Italian forces captured Berbera, capital of British Somaliland, on 19 August.
Goring ordered attacks on the British aircraft industry on 19 August.
The submarine U-104 was commissioned on 19 August.

weather: Generally cloudy with rain spreading from the north, the Channel mainly fine.
air: Activity was again reduced. In the afternoon a raid plotted at 190 aircraft crossed between Dover and Manston towards the Thames Estuary and Canterbury and was driven off, and twelve Bf 109s that tried to strafe Manston were driven off. Single aircraft attacked targets in East Anglia, a convoy east of Dunwich, and Llanreath, Neath and Port Talbot in South Wales. There was very little activity at night.
home: Churchill told the Commons on 20 August that never in the field of human conflict was so much owed by so many to so few.
Leon Trotsky was attacked with an ice axe at his home in Mexico City on 20 August.
Chinese Communist forces opened the Hundred Regiments Offensive against the Japanese in north China on 20 August.
reich: Italy announced a blockade of British ports in the Mediterranean on 20 August.
The submarine U-141 was commissioned on 20 August.
UA sank the Panamanian steamer Tuira from convoy OB-198 on 20 August.

weather: Cloudy with occasional rain.
air: About 200 small raids, mostly by single aircraft, crossed the east and south coasts and made short runs inland, mainly against airfields in East Anglia and along the south coast. Ju 88s bombed the Coastal Command airfield at St Eval in Cornwall. Fighters claimed thirteen raiders for the loss of one Hurricane, whose pilot was safe. There was very little activity at night.
home: Leon Trotsky died in Mexico City on 21 August of wounds received the day before.
The Congress Working Committee, meeting at Wardha on 21 August, rejected the Viceroy's August Offer.
reich: Leon Trotsky died in Mexico on 21 August after being attacked by a Soviet agent the previous day.

weather: Cloudy and squally.
air: Convoy Totem was shelled in the Dover Straits around midday by German heavy guns near Cap Gris Nez, without hits, and was then attacked by about 30 aircraft. In the evening further raids crossed near Deal, and Dover, Deal and Manston were bombed. Night activity increased over the Midlands, the north and the west, and bombs fell at Harrow at about 0330, the first inside the London Civil Defence Area.
home: Bombs fell on Harrow in the early hours of 22 August, the first within the London Civil Defence Area.
The physicist Sir Oliver Lodge died on 22 August aged 89.
The Allied Forces Act of 22 August allowed exiled governments to maintain their own armed forces on British soil.
reich: German long range coastal guns near Cap Gris Nez fired on a British convoy in the Dover Straits on 22 August, and shelled Dover that evening.

weather: Showers with bright intervals, cloudy in the Straits, Channel and Thames Estuary.
air: Activity was restricted by weather to single raiders and reconnaissance. One aircraft bombed and machine gunned targets near Rugby and Warwick. A He 111 was destroyed near Sumburgh, a Ju 88 near Weymouth, and a reconnaissance aircraft was shot down by anti-aircraft fire at Duxford and its crew of five captured. At night the main attacks fell on South Wales, with Cardiff visited several times.
home: King George VI ordered on 23 August that all Germans and Italians be removed from the lists of British titles and decorations.
The destroyer HMS Hostile struck a mine off Cape Bon, Tunisia, on 23 August and had to be scuttled.
reich: U-37 sank the British steamer Severn Leigh and the Norwegian Keret from convoy OA-200 on 23 August.
The British destroyer Hostile was lost on a mine off Cape Bon on 23 August.

weather: Fine and clear in the south, drizzle in the north.
air: Six large raids crossed the Kent coast during the day. Manston was bombed repeatedly and was evacuated as a fighter base, and Defiants of 264 Squadron were engaged over it. In the afternoon Hornchurch and North Weald were attacked, and a heavy raid on Portsmouth killed more than 100 people. At night bombs fell on the City of London, Millwall, Tottenham and Islington, and Birmingham was raided for four hours.
home: More than 100 people were killed and 300 injured in a raid on Portsmouth on 24 August.
Florey, Chain and Heatley of Oxford published their penicillin results in The Lancet on 24 August.
reich: The battleship Bismarck was commissioned on 24 August.
U-37 sank the British sloop HMS Penzance, escorting convoy SC-1, on 24 August.
U-57 torpedoed three ships of convoy OB-202 on 24 August, sinking the Cumberland and the Saint Dunstan.

weather: Fair in the early morning, cloudy for the rest of the day.
air: Activity was slight until late afternoon, when mass raids from the Cherbourg area crossed to Weymouth and Portland and Ju 88s bombed Warmwell airfield. In the evening formations from Calais attacked East Kent, the Isle of Sheppey and the Thames Estuary. Night raids were on a large scale, chiefly against South Wales, Bristol, Birmingham and Coventry. RAF bombers flew to Berlin that night.
home: Bombs fell on the City and other parts of London during the night of 24 to 25 August.
Prince Jean, Duke of Guise, Orleanist claimant to the French throne, died on 25 August.
reich: U-48 and U-124 attacked convoy HX-65A on 25 August and sank four British ships, including the tanker Athelcrest.
U-57 sank the British tanker Pecten from convoy HX-65B on 25 August.

weather: Mainly cloudy but dry, brighter in the south.
air: Three major attacks developed. At about 1140 some 100 aircraft attacked the Dover and Folkestone area and pressed towards Biggin Hill and Kenley. At 1422 about 190 aircraft crossed between Lympne and the Blackwater to attack airfields north and south of the Thames Estuary. At 1600 Portsmouth and Southampton were raided. No. 1 Squadron RCAF fought its first action. Night raids on Birmingham and Coventry were heavy.
home: RAF bombers attacked Berlin for the first time on the night of 25 to 26 August.
The French colony of Chad declared for Free France on 26 August.
German aircraft bombed Campile in County Wexford, in neutral Ireland, on 26 August, killing three women.
reich: British bombers raided Berlin for the first time on the night of 25 to 26 August. Damage was slight and nobody was killed.
German bombs fell on County Wexford in neutral Ireland on 26 August, killing three women, and the Irish government protested.
The French colony of Chad went over to de Gaulle on 26 August.

weather: Rain in central and eastern England, some cloud in the Channel and haze over the Dover Straits.
air: Daylight activity was limited to reconnaissance flights, chiefly in the Portsmouth and Southampton area. Several of these aircraft were intercepted and destroyed, including a Dornier near Dover and others near Chelmsford and Warmwell. Night raids were scattered over most of the country, including the Midlands, East Anglia, Kent, South Wales, Chatham and Portsmouth, and London had two red warnings.
home: Free French forces under Leclerc took control of Douala in French Cameroon on 27 August.
President Roosevelt signed a resolution on 27 August allowing him to call the National Guard and Army Reserve into service for a year.
reich: U-46 torpedoed the British armed merchant cruiser Dunvegan Castle, escorting convoy SL-43, on 27 August.
U-28 sank the Norwegian steamer Eva from convoy SC-1 on 27 August.

weather: Fine and fair but cold, with cloud in the Dover Straits.
air: Four major attacks crossed Kent. In the morning bombers with Bf 109 escort made for Eastchurch and Rochford, and Defiants of 264 Squadron were again in action. At about 1300 some 100 aircraft flew to the Thames Estuary and Rochford was bombed. Later waves of more than 100 aircraft swept over Kent and the Estuary. That night about 150 bombers made the first major attack on Liverpool.
home: French Congo and Ubangi-Shari declared for Free France on 28 August.
Liverpool had its first major night air raid on 28 August.
reich: The submarine U-94 was commissioned on 28 August.
U-101 sank the Finnish steamer Elle from convoy SC-1 and U-28 sank the British steamer Kyno from convoy HX-66 on 28 August.
French Congo and Ubangi-Shari went over to de Gaulle on 28 August.

weather: Showers and bright intervals, with cloud in the Channel and Straits.
air: The morning was quiet apart from a small raid on Warmwell. At about 1510 a formation of some 170 aircraft, largely fighters, crossed near Dover and headed towards Biggin Hill but was driven off without bombing being reported. At 1725 a smaller raid flew over the North Foreland towards Rochester. At night Liverpool was attacked again, with diversionary raids on the Midlands.
home: Germany formally apologised to Ireland on 29 August for the bombing in County Wexford three days earlier.
Liverpool was raided for the second night running on 29 August.
reich: U-100 under Joachim Schepke sank four ships of convoy OA-204 north-west of Ireland on 29 August and damaged a fifth.
The German government apologised to Ireland on 29 August for the bombs dropped in County Wexford.

weather: Fair.
air: After feints against shipping, waves of more than 100 aircraft crossed Kent from 1100 and attacked Biggin Hill, Eastchurch and targets in the Thames Estuary. Further formations in the afternoon made for Biggin Hill, Detling, Kenley, North Weald and Hornchurch, and at about 1610 He 111s bombed the Vauxhall works at Luton. Fighter Command flew 1,054 sorties. Liverpool was raided for the third night.
home: Germany and Italy awarded northern Transylvania to Hungary at Vienna on 30 August.
The physicist Sir J. J. Thomson, discoverer of the electron, died on 30 August aged 83.
Vichy France agreed on 30 August to allow Japanese troops to be stationed in Indochina.
reich: The Second Vienna Award of 30 August, arbitrated by Germany and Italy, transferred northern Transylvania from Romania to Hungary.
U-32 sank three ships of convoy HX-66A on 30 August.
The submarine U-93 was commissioned on 30 August.

weather: Mainly fair, with haze over the Thames Estuary and Dover Straits.
air: From about 0800 some 250 aircraft in five waves attacked North Weald, Debden, Duxford, Eastchurch and Detling, and Bf 109s shot down all 23 balloons of the Dover barrage. Around midday Biggin Hill was damaged and Hornchurch and Debden attacked, and at 1800 about 200 aircraft raided Hornchurch and Biggin Hill again. Fighter Command had its heaviest losses of the battle. At night Liverpool was the main target.
home: President Roosevelt called 60,000 National Guardsmen into federal service on 31 August.
Two Royal Navy destroyers were lost in a minefield off Texel on the Dutch coast on the night of 31 August.
Laurence Olivier and Vivien Leigh were married in California on 31 August.
reich: U-60 torpedoed and damaged the Dutch liner Volendam of 15,434 tons in convoy OB-205 on 31 August.
Two British destroyers were sunk in a minefield off Texel on the night of 31 August.
The submarine U-95 was commissioned on 31 August.

weather: Fair with patches of cloud in the morning, clearing in the afternoon.
air: The Luftwaffe made four main attacks on Fighter Command airfields in Kent and the Thames Estuary. Biggin Hill was hit again and its operations room wrecked, Kenley and Detling were damaged and Tilbury docks were bombed. After dark Liverpool was raided again, with smaller raids on South Wales and the Midlands.
home: Romania ceded Northern Transylvania to Hungary under the Vienna Award of 30 August, arbitrated by Germany and Italy.
Liverpool was bombed again overnight, continuing the run of night raids on Merseyside that began on 28 August.
reich: The Second Vienna Award of 30 August, arbitrated by Germany and Italy, transferred Northern Transylvania from Romania to Hungary.
U-32 torpedoed and damaged the British cruiser Fiji north west of Ireland on 1 September.

weather: Fine and warm after early morning mist and fog patches.
air: Successive waves attacked airfields in Kent and Essex, among them Eastchurch, Detling, Hornchurch, North Weald, Biggin Hill and Gravesend, and the Short Brothers works at Rochester was bombed. At night scattered raiders reached Liverpool, the Midlands and South Wales, where Swansea was hit hard.
home: Britain and the United States exchanged notes in Washington on 2 September giving Britain 50 old destroyers in return for leases on Atlantic bases.
reich: Göring met his fighter commanders in France on 2 September to discuss bomber escort and losses.
U-46 and U-47 sank the steamers Thornlea and Ville de Mons in the Atlantic approaches on 2 September.

weather: Fine and warm in the south with haze in the Channel and Straits. Cloud and drizzle in the north.
air: A morning attack by Do 17s with Bf 110 and Bf 109 escort struck North Weald, where more than 150 bombs fell, and Hornchurch and Debden were also targets. A smaller raid followed in the early afternoon. Pilot Officer Richard Hillary of 603 Squadron was shot down and badly burned. At night Liverpool was bombed again, with raids on South Wales and Avonmouth.
home: Tuesday 3 September was the first anniversary of Britain's declaration of war on Germany.
President Roosevelt told Congress on 3 September of the transfer of 50 destroyers to Britain in exchange for base leases.
reich: An OKW directive of 3 September set 20 September as the earliest sailing date and 21 September as the landing day for Operation Sea Lion.
Vichy France ordered on 3 September the internment of persons judged a danger to national security.

weather: Fine and warm with haze in the Channel and Straits. Rain and strong winds in the north.
air: Two main attacks crossed Kent and the Thames Estuary towards the fighter airfields. At about 13:30 Bf 110 fighter bombers bombed the Vickers works at Brooklands, killing more than 80 workers and halting Wellington production for several days. At night Liverpool, Bristol, South Wales and Tyneside were raided.
home: German motor torpedo boats sank several colliers from an east coast convoy off Norfolk on the night of 4 September.
King Carol of Romania asked General Ion Antonescu on 4 September to form a government.
reich: Hitler spoke at the Berlin Sportpalast on 4 September, opening the winter relief campaign and threatening heavy reprisal raids on British cities.
Motor torpedo boats attacked convoy FS 271 off the Norfolk coast and sank several steamers.

weather: Fine and warm again, with cloud building later.
air: A morning raid of about 70 aircraft crossed at Dungeness and Biggin Hill was damaged again. In the afternoon Ju 88s and He 111s under heavy Bf 109 escort bombed the oil depot at Thameshaven, starting fires visible from London. 303 (Polish) Squadron was among the units engaged. At night raids reached London, Kent, Essex, Liverpool and North Wales.
home: Churchill told the Commons on 5 September that 1,075 civilians were killed in air raids during August, and widened compensation for bomb damage.
He also confirmed to the House the agreement with the United States for the transfer of 50 destroyers.
reich: King Carol of Romania granted General Antonescu full powers on 5 September.
Hungarian troops began entering Northern Transylvania on 5 September under the Vienna Award.

weather: Fine but cooler, with haze in the Straits and the Thames Estuary.
air: Three main attacks crossed Kent and the Thames Estuary towards Biggin Hill, North Weald, Hornchurch and the oil tanks at Thameshaven. 303 (Polish) Squadron lost several Hurricanes in the morning fight. After dark bombs fell on the London docks area, West Ham, Woolwich and Southwark.
home: King Carol II of Romania abdicated on 6 September in favour of his son Michael, with General Antonescu holding power.
The first eight American destroyers reached Halifax, Nova Scotia, on 6 September for handing over to the Royal Navy.
The King and Queen visited Fighter Command headquarters at Bentley Priory on 6 September.
reich: King Carol II of Romania abdicated on 6 September. His son Michael succeeded him and General Antonescu took control of the government.

weather: Fair with some haze.
air: After a morning raid on Hawkinge and Dover, about 350 aircraft flew up the Thames late in the afternoon and bombed the London docks, Woolwich Arsenal, Beckton gasworks, West Ham and Thameshaven. Night bombers guided by the fires attacked the East End until dawn. More than 400 Londoners were killed and over 1,300 seriously injured.
home: GHQ Home Forces issued the code word Cromwell on the evening of 7 September, bringing troops to immediate readiness for invasion.
Bulgaria and Romania signed the Treaty of Craiova on 7 September, returning Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria.
reich: Göring, on the Channel coast, announced on 7 September that he had taken personal command of the air attacks on England.
Bulgaria and Romania signed the Treaty of Craiova on 7 September, returning Southern Dobruja to Bulgaria.
U-47 sank three ships of convoy SC 2 in the North Atlantic on 7 September.

weather: Fair early and in the evening, cloudy for the rest of the day.
air: Daylight activity was slight. About 20 Do 17s with Bf 109 escort crossed near Deal before midday and were intercepted, their bombs falling across Kent, including West Malling and Detling. From about 20:00 until dawn some 250 bombers attacked London again, hitting the docks, railway termini and hospitals. About 400 civilians were killed.
home: A National Day of Prayer was observed on Sunday 8 September, with the King and Queen at the service in Westminster Abbey.
Church bells were rung in some districts during the night of 7 September in the mistaken belief that invasion had begun.
reich: In Vichy France, Daladier, Reynaud and General Gamelin were arrested and interned on 7 September.
Marshal Graziani agreed on 8 September to open the Italian offensive from Libya into Egypt.

weather: Scattered showers, thundery in the east. Fair over the Channel.
air: In the late afternoon about 300 aircraft headed for London, the Thames Estuary and the aircraft factories south west of the capital. They were met over Kent and Surrey, and most bombers dropped their loads short of their targets. The Duxford wing was engaged. At night London was the main target, with fires in the City around St Paul's.
home: Italian aircraft bombed Tel Aviv on 9 September, killing more than 100 people.
The first American destroyers were taken over by the Royal Navy at Halifax on 9 September.
The King toured bombed districts of the East End on 9 September.
reich: Italian aircraft bombed Tel Aviv in Palestine on 9 September.
U-47 and U-28 sank further ships from convoy SC 2 in the North Atlantic.

weather: Generally cloudy with some rain.
air: Cloud and rain limited operations to single aircraft raids. Tangmere, West Malling and Poling were attacked, and a Do 17 of KG 76 was shot down over Sussex by Spitfires of 72 and 92 Squadrons. At night more than 150 bombers attacked London, starting large fires at St Katharine Docks, with lesser raids on Merseyside and South Wales.
home: A delayed action bomb that had fallen at Buckingham Palace exploded on 10 September and damaged the building.
reich: Italy formed the Corpo Aereo Italiano on 10 September to take part in the air campaign against Britain.
Hitler deferred his decision on Operation Sea Lion on 10 September and set 14 September for the next review.

weather: Mainly fine with local showers. Cloud in the Channel and the Thames Estuary.
air: In mid afternoon about 250 aircraft crossed Kent and some 30 reached central London, bombing the docks, Woolwich and Lewisham. At the same time a raid on the Portsmouth and Southampton area hit the Cunliffe Owen works at Eastleigh, killing about 50. Both sides lost about the same number of aircraft. London and Merseyside were bombed at night.
home: Churchill broadcast on the evening of 11 September, warning that an invasion attempt might come soon and calling the coming week critical.
reich: With the decision on Operation Sea Lion put off until 14 September, the earliest possible landing date moved to 24 September.

weather: Unsettled, with rain in most districts.
air: Rain kept activity to reconnaissance and single raiders. Bombs fell at Harrogate, Hastings and around south London, and one raider was shot down. Wing Commander J. S. Dewar was lost on a flight to Tangmere. The night raid on London was much lighter, by about 50 bombers. A large delayed action bomb lodged close to St Paul's Cathedral.
home: Royal Engineers began digging out a large unexploded bomb buried close to St Paul's Cathedral.
RAF bombers attacked the invasion barges gathered in the Channel ports on 12 September.
reich: Hungarian forces were completing the occupation of Northern Transylvania, begun on 5 September under the Vienna Award.

weather: Unsettled, with cloud and poor visibility.
air: Small raids, mostly single aircraft using cloud cover, came in over Kent to London through the day. At about 11:00 a bomber hit Buckingham Palace, wrecking the chapel while the King and Queen were in residence. Whitehall, Maidstone and Eastbourne were also bombed. Sergeant J. H. Lacey of 501 Squadron shot down a He 111 and baled out. London was bombed again at night.
home: Buckingham Palace was bombed in daylight on 13 September while the King and Queen were there. The chapel was wrecked and neither was hurt.
Italian forces crossed the frontier from Libya into Egypt on 13 September and occupied Sollum.
reich: The Italian Tenth Army crossed from Libya into Egypt on 13 September, retaking Fort Capuzzo and occupying Sollum.
Hitler met his commanders in Berlin on 13 September to review the air offensive and the invasion plans.

weather: Showers and local thunder. Cloud in the Straits, the Channel and the Thames Estuary.
air: Two afternoon attacks, of about 150 and 100 aircraft and made up largely of fighters, came in over Kent and the Thames Estuary towards London. Coastal towns including Brighton and Eastbourne were bombed by single raiders. 73 Squadron lost three Hurricanes. Night activity was reduced, with London again the main target.
home: RAF Bomber Command sent heavy raids against Antwerp and the invasion barges in the Channel ports on the night of 14 September.
reich: Hitler reviewed Operation Sea Lion on 14 September and put off the decision for a further three days, to 17 September.

weather: Fair with some cloud patches, fine in the evening.
air: Two large attacks were made on London, the first about midday and the second in mid afternoon, and both were met in strength by 11 Group and the Duxford wing. Bombs fell across south and east London. Smaller raids attacked Portland and the Supermarine works at Woolston. Sergeant R. T. Holmes of 504 Squadron brought down a Dornier that fell on Victoria Station. London was bombed again at night.
home: The Prime Minister watched the battle of 15 September from the 11 Group operations room at Uxbridge.
RAF bombers attacked the invasion ports that night. Sergeant John Hannah of 83 Squadron fought a fire aboard his Hampden over Antwerp.
reich: U-48 sank the British sloop Dundee, an escort of convoy SC 3, west of Ireland on 15 September.
The battleship Bismarck left Hamburg for the first time on 15 September.

weather: General rain and cloud.
air: A force of several hundred aircraft assembled over the Pas de Calais early in the morning and crossed into Kent, but turned back without pressing on to London. Rain and cloud prevented almost all further fighting. After dark London was bombed continuously, with smaller raids on Merseyside and the Midlands.
home: President Roosevelt signed the Selective Training and Service Act on 16 September, the first peacetime conscription in the United States.
Aircraft from the carrier Illustrious attacked Benghazi harbour on the night of 16 September and sank Italian ships.
reich: Italian forces occupied Sidi Barrani in Egypt on 16 September and halted there.
Göring conferred with his air fleet commanders on 16 September after the losses of the previous day.
Spanish minister Ramon Serrano Suner was in Berlin on 16 September for talks with Ribbentrop.

weather: Squally showers with thunder and bright intervals.
air: Showers kept the morning quiet. At about 15:30 a large fighter sweep crossed the Kent coast and was met by many squadrons, with fighting over east Kent. At night London was heavily bombed and parachute mines were used. Oxford Street stores including John Lewis were burned out. Merseyside and Glasgow were also raided.
home: Churchill told the Commons on 17 September that about 2,000 civilians had been killed and 8,000 wounded in the first half of the month, most in London.
The House then went into secret session.
reich: Hitler postponed Operation Sea Lion until further notice on 17 September.
Spanish minister Ramon Serrano Suner was received by Hitler in Berlin on 17 September.

weather: Bright and squally.
air: Several raids crossed Kent and the Estuary during the day, the first made up mostly of fighters. In the late afternoon bombers making for Tilbury and the Thames docks were intercepted by the Duxford wing led by Squadron Leader Bader and lost several aircraft. Chatham, Sheerness and the Maidstone area were bombed. At night London was hit hard again and Merseyside was raided.
home: Large fires burned in Oxford Street after the night raid of 17 September, which gutted the John Lewis store.
reich: U-48 torpedoed and sank the British liner City of Benares in convoy OB 213 in the North Atlantic late on 17 September.

weather: Showery.
air: There were no major attacks. Single raiders operated over the south east, the Thames Estuary and east London, and several Ju 88s were shot down. One Ju 88 force landed intact at Oakington in Cambridgeshire. At night London and Merseyside were bombed. Heston aerodrome was damaged and a public shelter in Tottenham was hit.
home: No. 71 Squadron, the first Eagle squadron of American volunteer pilots, formed at Church Fenton on 19 September.
RAF bombers kept up their night attacks on the invasion barges in the Channel ports.
reich: Hitler ordered on 19 September that the assembly of invasion shipping stop and that vessels in the Channel ports be dispersed.
Ribbentrop was in Rome on 19 September for talks with Mussolini.

weather: Fair with bright periods and showers.
air: At about 11:00 a force of roughly 100 aircraft, mostly Bf 109s and some of them carrying bombs, swept over east Kent towards London. Bombs fell near the Thames by London Bridge. Spitfire squadrons including 72, 92 and 222 lost several aircraft to the high flying fighters. London was the target again at night.
home: Ministers were reconsidering the ban on sheltering in Underground stations, which many Londoners were already using at night.
reich: Major Werner Mölders of JG 51 claimed his 40th victory on 20 September.
U-47 sighted convoy HX 72 in the North Atlantic on 20 September and other boats were called in.

weather: Mainly fine.
air: Only reconnaissance aircraft and single raiders appeared until about 18:00, when some 200 aircraft, mostly fighters, swept over Kent and the Estuary and a few reached the eastern edge of London. Single German aircraft were shot down in Sussex and near Liverpool. At night London and Merseyside were attacked.
home: The government gave official approval on 21 September for Underground stations to be used as air raid shelters.
Australia voted in a federal election on 21 September. The Menzies government stayed in office.
reich: Major Werner Mölders was awarded the Oak Leaves to the Knight's Cross on 21 September after his 40th victory.
U-boats including U-47, U-99 and U-100 attacked convoy HX 72 west of Ireland on the night of 21 September.

weather: Dull with fog in the morning, some rain, clearing later in the afternoon.
air: Fog and cloud made this one of the quietest days of the battle and Fighter Command flew very few sorties. Two raiders flew inland to the Duxford area, and a Ju 88 was shot down off Cornwall by 234 Squadron. After dark London was heavily attacked, with large fires in the docks and at Woolwich and direct hits on shelters in Poplar and Lambeth.
home: Japanese troops began moving into northern French Indochina on 22 September after the French authorities at Hanoi accepted Japanese demands.
RAF bombers attacked Berlin on the night of 22 September.
reich: The attack on convoy HX 72 ended on 22 September with 11 ships sunk.
Japan and Vichy France signed an agreement at Hanoi on 22 September admitting Japanese troops to northern Indochina.
Germany and Finland agreed on 22 September on the transit of German troops through Finland to northern Norway.

weather: Fine.
air: At about 09:30 some 200 aircraft, nearly all Bf 109s, swept over east Kent and the Estuary and were met by 11 Group without reaching London. A second, smaller sweep came in over Kent at about 17:30. The fighting was fighter against fighter. At night London was bombed from 19:45, West Ham suffering badly, and Merseyside was also raided.
home: The King broadcast on 23 September and announced the creation of the George Cross and George Medal for civilian gallantry.
News was released that the liner City of Benares had been sunk in the Atlantic on 17 September with the loss of 77 evacuee children.
British and Free French forces under General de Gaulle arrived off Dakar on 23 September and were fired on by the Vichy garrison.
reich: Vichy French forces at Dakar resisted a British and Free French landing attempt that began on 23 September.
About 120 RAF bombers were sent against Berlin on the night of 23 September.

weather: Early fog in northern France. Channel cloudy, with haze in the Straits and the Thames Estuary.
air: Two morning attacks of about 200 aircraft crossed Kent towards Tilbury and Gravesend, and many turned back early. At about 13:30 Bf 110 fighter bombers attacked the Supermarine works at Woolston, Southampton, where a works shelter was hit with heavy loss of life. A second raid reached the Southampton area later. London and Merseyside were bombed at night.
home: Vichy French aircraft bombed Gibraltar on 24 September in reprisal for the attack on Dakar.
Fighting continued off Dakar, where the battleship Richelieu and the shore batteries engaged the British squadron.
reich: Vichy French bombers from Morocco and Algeria attacked Gibraltar on 24 September in reply to the Dakar operation.
Major Adolf Galland of JG 26 claimed his 40th victory on 24 September.

weather: Fair to fine in most areas, and cool.
air: Late in the morning a force of He 111s with Bf 110 escort flew in over the Dorset coast and bombed the Bristol Aeroplane Company works at Filton, causing heavy damage and killing about 130 people, most of them workers. Portland and later Plymouth were also attacked. 504 Squadron was moved to Filton afterwards. At night London, North Wales and Lancashire were bombed.
home: The British and Free French force broke off the attack on Dakar on 25 September after the battleship Resolution was torpedoed.
Vichy aircraft bombed Gibraltar for a second day on 25 September.
reich: Reichskommissar Terboven announced on 25 September that all Norwegian parties except Nasjonal Samling were banned.
Major Adolf Galland received the Oak Leaves to the Knight's Cross on 25 September.
The British and Free French attempt on Dakar was abandoned on 25 September.

weather: Mainly fair to cloudy.
air: At about 16:30 a force of He 111s and Bf 110s bombed the Supermarine works at Woolston, Southampton, wrecking the factory and killing many people in the town. At dusk about 25 bombers attacked Crewe. 303 (Polish) Squadron was in action during a visit by the King to Northolt. London and Merseyside were raided at night.
home: The King visited RAF Northolt on 26 September while 303 (Polish) Squadron was in action.
The United States announced on 26 September an embargo on exports of scrap iron and steel, to take effect on 16 October.
reich: Grand Admiral Raeder urged Hitler on 26 September to turn the war effort towards the Mediterranean, against Gibraltar and Suez.
Japanese forces completed their occupation of northern French Indochina on 26 September.

weather: Fair in the far south and south west. Cloud in the Channel and light rain over southern England.
air: Three major attacks were made on London and the south east, and a smaller force made for Filton. The raids were met over Kent and Surrey and few bombers reached London. Hauptmann Martin Lutz, leading Erprobungsgruppe 210, was killed. A Ju 88 crew that force landed on Graveney Marsh in Kent exchanged fire with soldiers before surrendering. London, Merseyside and the Midlands were bombed at night.
home: Germany, Italy and Japan signed a ten year military and economic pact in Berlin on 27 September.
In Washington, Secretary of State Cordell Hull played down the significance of the pact.
reich: Germany, Italy and Japan signed the Tripartite Pact in Berlin on 27 September. Ribbentrop, Ciano and Ambassador Kurusu signed.

weather: Fair to fine inland. Cloud over the Channel, the Straits and the Thames Estuary.
air: Two attacks came over Kent towards London and one approached Portsmouth, made up mostly of fighters flying very high, with few bombers. Some bombs fell on Poplar, Deptford and Woolwich. Fighter Command lost more aircraft than it shot down. Flying Officer A. G. Lewis of 249 Squadron was shot down and badly burned. London was bombed again at night.
home: The first of the 50 American destroyers reached Britain on 28 September.
Radio Belgique began broadcasting from London to occupied Belgium on 28 September.
reich: Count Ciano was received by Hitler in Berlin on 28 September, the day after the pact was signed.
The battleship Bismarck left Kiel on 28 September for trials in the Baltic.

weather: Fine early and late, cloudy in between.
air: Activity was reduced. Reconnaissance aircraft and single raiders operated over East Anglia and the south, and convoys were attacked. In the late afternoon fighter formations swept through Kent and one element flew as far as Reading. At night London and Merseyside were bombed, and He 111s of KG 27 started dock fires in Liverpool.
home: British warships bombarded the Italian held coast road in Libya on 29 September.
reich: U-32 sank the British steamer Bassa south west of Rockall on 29 September.

weather: Generally fair but cloudy, with light winds.
air: Four attacks, strong in fighters, crossed Kent towards London and two approached the Dorset coast, one of them making for Yeovil. Most were broken up and few bombs fell on London by day. After dark about 175 aircraft reached central London, and raids also went to Merseyside, the Midlands and South Wales.
home: The first awards of the George Cross were gazetted on 30 September, among them Lieutenant R. Davies and Sapper G. Wyllie for the St Paul's bomb.
Three German agents landed by seaplane on the Moray coast on 30 September and were arrested within a day.
reich: Berlin schoolchildren were offered extended holidays from 30 September if their parents placed them in the country.
The submarine U-73 was commissioned on 30 September.

weather: Mainly fair but generally cloudy.
air: Bf 109s of JG 2 and JG 53 with Bf 110s of ZG 26 swept the Portsmouth and Southampton area in the morning, and three waves of fighters and fighter bombers came in over Kent towards London in the afternoon. RAF Carew Cheriton in Wales was bombed at dawn. At night London was the main target, with Manchester, Birkenhead and other towns also hit.
home: The first of the American destroyers transferred to the Royal Navy reached Britain on 28 September.
British warships bombarded the coastal road in Italian Libya on 29 September.
reich: U-38 torpedoed and sank the British motor ship Highland Patriot, 14,172 tons, in the Atlantic on 1 October.
Berlin schoolchildren were told on 30 September that holidays would be extended for those whose parents placed them in the country.

weather: Clear skies by day, with cloud building up later.
air: Six raids, mostly of Bf 109s and Bf 110s with some Ju 88s and Do 17s, crossed south east England and bombs fell on Woolwich, Camberwell, Rochester and several coastal towns. A Ju 88 on a weather and reconnaissance flight lost its way and landed intact at Brightlingsea in Essex. London was again the main night target, and Manchester and Aberdeen were also raided.
home: British destroyers attacked the Italian submarine Berillo in the Mediterranean on 2 October and her crew scuttled her.
reich: Night bombers again made London their main target on the night of 2 October, with Manchester also attacked.

weather: Rain and drizzle in the Channel, with visibility down to 500 yards in places.
air: In poor weather single aircraft made scattered low level raids on airfields, factories and railways. A Ju 88 bombed the de Havilland works at Hatfield, killing 21 people, and was shot down by the ground defences. Night activity was much reduced, with London the main target and the General Aircraft works at Feltham damaged.
home: Mr Neville Chamberlain resigned as Lord President of the Council on 3 October because of failing health.

weather: Mist, rain and poor visibility all day, with fog at night.
air: Single aircraft and small formations raided London and the south east through the murk, with activity heaviest around mid afternoon. Bombs hit the New Cross telephone exchange, Euston station and the Hawker factory at Kingston. After dark more than 100 bombers crossed in a stream towards London, and Liverpool and Bristol were also raided.
home: In the Cabinet changes Sir John Anderson became Lord President and Mr Herbert Morrison became Home Secretary.
Mr Ernest Bevin and Sir Kingsley Wood joined the War Cabinet.
reich: Hitler and Mussolini met at the Brenner Pass on 4 October to discuss the conduct of the war, including the position of Spain.

weather: Local showers in most parts with bright periods, winds light and variable.
air: Six attacks were made on Kent, London and the Portsmouth and Southampton area, the largest of about 150 aircraft crossing near Lympne in the morning. No. 303 (Polish) Squadron fought Bf 110s and Bf 109s over West Malling, and Ju 88s with a Bf 109 escort attacked Southampton in the afternoon. Fighter Command flew 1,175 sorties. London was raided again at night.
home: Hitler and Mussolini conferred at the Brenner Pass on 4 October.
reich: Helmut Wick of JG 2 claimed five British fighters in the fighting over the south coast on 5 October.

weather: Dull, with continuous rain all day.
air: Poor visibility ruled out formation attacks, and lone aircraft raided airfields, towns and convoys in East Anglia, Kent and Sussex. A Ju 88 bombed Northolt, destroying a Hurricane of No. 303 Squadron and killing Sergeant Siudak, and Biggin Hill, Croydon and Tangmere were also attacked. Heavy cloud made the night very quiet.
home: Air Marshal Sir Richard Peirse took over Bomber Command from Sir Charles Portal on 5 October.
reich: Mussolini inspected units of the Italian armed forces in northern Italy on 6 October.
Werner Moelders of JG 51 flew the new Bf 109 F on operations for the first time on 6 October.

weather: Occasional showers, fair visibility and variable cloud.
air: Large fighter and fighter bomber formations crossed Kent towards London and Biggin Hill from mid morning, and No. 11 Group put up 16 squadrons against the first sweep. In the afternoon Ju 88s of KG 51 escorted by Bf 110s and Bf 109s bombed the Westland works at Yeovil, where an air raid shelter was hit. At night raids reached the Midlands, Lancashire, Tyneside and the Forth as well as London.
home: Heavy cloud on the night of 6 October kept raiding over London to a few scattered aircraft.
reich: Oberleutnant Viktor Moelders of JG 51 was shot down over England on 7 October during a fighter bomber attack on London and taken prisoner.

weather: Cloudy but fair in the south east, with high winds.
air: Fighter bombers reached central London soon after 8.30 am, followed by a second wave of more than 100 aircraft. Bombs fell near Charing Cross, the Air Ministry and BBC buildings, and on Bermondsey, Lewisham and West Ham. Sergeant Josef Frantisek of No. 303 Squadron was killed in a crash at Ewell. No. 312 (Czech) Squadron shot down a Ju 88 near Speke. London was the main target at night.
home: Mr Churchill reviewed the war in the Commons on 8 October, dealing with the air battle, Dakar, Vichy France and the Burma Road.
RAF bombers attacked targets in Berlin on the night of 7 October, the heaviest raid on the city so far.
reich: German troops entered Romania to train the Romanian army and guard the oilfields.
British bombers attacked Berlin on the night of 7 to 8 October.

weather: Cloudy in the Channel, with rain over northern France and the Straits of Dover.
air: No. 1 Squadron shot down a Ju 88 over the Wash in the morning. The main attack came in mid afternoon, when 160 to 180 aircraft headed for east London, Hornchurch and Biggin Hill, and fighter bombers hit Maidstone, Hastings and East Ham. At night about 90 bombers attacked London, where railways were hit and St Paul's Cathedral was damaged. Mines were laid off the east coast.
home: Mr Churchill was elected leader of the Conservative Party on 9 October in succession to Mr Chamberlain.
General de Gaulle arrived at Douala in the French Cameroons on 8 October.
reich: U-103 sank three ships from convoy SC 6 in the North Atlantic on 9 October.

weather: Showery with bright intervals, haze in the Thames Estuary and East Anglia.
air: Hastings and Dover were bombed early, and fighter formations crossed Kent through the day. No. 92 Squadron lost three Spitfires near Brighton. Around midday more than 100 aircraft approached the Dorset coast near Lulworth and were met by No. 10 Group squadrons. At night London, Manchester and fifteen airfields were attacked.
home: A bomb struck St Paul's Cathedral in the night raid of 9 October, damaging the choir and the high altar.
reich: Hitler ordered an emergency programme of air raid shelter building for German cities on 10 October.
U-48 torpedoed ships of convoy HX 77 in the North Atlantic on 10 October.

weather: Mainly fair apart from coastal showers, with fog forming at night.
air: Several waves of fighters and fighter bombers, more than 190 aircraft in all, came in over Kent, Sussex and the Thames Estuary, with JG 26 and JG 53 aircraft bombing Hastings, Folkestone and Whitstable. Afternoon raids headed for London and Portland. At night London, Liverpool, Manchester and Tyneside were bombed, and the Centre Court at Wimbledon was hit.
home: The battleship HMS Revenge and six destroyers bombarded the harbour at Cherbourg in the night of 10 to 11 October.
reich: British warships shelled Cherbourg in the night of 10 to 11 October.
Marshal Petain spoke on French radio on 11 October about France's future relations with her neighbours.

weather: Widespread mist and fog, clearing later.
air: Once the fog lifted Bf 109 fighter bombers made repeated attacks on London and the Home Counties, with fighting over north Kent, Hastings and the Thames Estuary. No. 145 Squadron destroyed an Arado 196 seaplane and was in action with Bf 109s of JG 51. At night London was bombed from 7.20 pm, a bomb in Trafalgar Square killing seven people, and Coventry was heavily attacked.
home: The Centre Court at Wimbledon was hit by a bomb during the night raid of 11 October.
reich: A directive of 12 October put off the planned landing in England until the spring of 1941 at the earliest.
Werner Moelders of JG 51 claimed three Hurricanes on 12 October, bringing his total to 45.

weather: Early fog clearing to blue skies, cloud later.
air: From about 12.45 pm to 4 pm waves of 25 to 30 Bf 109s attacked London, hitting Woolwich and railway junctions at Dalston and Hackney. At night about 60 raids were plotted against London, Merseyside, Birmingham, Bristol and the north east. A shelter under flats in Stoke Newington collapsed, and 21 people died when a communal shelter in Middlesbrough was hit.
home: Princess Elizabeth made her first broadcast on 13 October, speaking to evacuated children on the BBC Children's Hour.
The Royal Navy sank the Italian ships Airone, Ariel and Artigliere off Cape Passero, south east of Sicily, on 12 October.
reich: U-48, U-59 and U-101 sank ships of convoy HX 77 in the North Atlantic on 12 October.

weather: Occasional rain or drizzle spreading to the south east, clearing to a moonlit night.
